units.la: Pontificem Romanum nisi sanctitatem Petri vere imitetur, nul- lam ex promissu Petro factis sibi afferre posse.
units.tr: The Roman Pontiff, unless he truly imitates the holiness of Peter, cannot claim for himself any promise made to Peter.

units.la: Dixit Christus [Porta inferi non praevalebunt adversus eam,] id est Petram, (inquis;) Recte: Ergo non adversus Petrum; verum id quoque, sed non quia Petrus ipsa Petra est, ipsumque aedificij fundamentum (qui honor soli Christo est deferendus) sed quia Petrus est saxum aedificatum supra ipsam Petram. Et, per [Porta inferorum] ut erudite admodum Maldonatus Iesuita) {t}Intelligitur simpliciter, absque omni restrictione, omnis Diaboli potentia; sive per Haereses, ut Epiphanius; sive per alia vitia, ut Ambrosius; sive per utraque, ut Origenes, Hieronymus, Beda; sive per blasphemias Haereticorum, ut Euthymius; sive per Persecutiones, ut Theophylactus; sive per blandimenta vitiosa, ut {u}Rabanus docuit. Enucleatam huius rationem Abulensis vester tradidit. {x}Porta accipiuntur (inquit) per Metaphoram, quia per portam intratur in Domum, ita id, quod ad inferos ducit, porta inferi dicitur: & quia homo trahitur ad inferos immediate per peccatum, mediate vero per passiones, quibus ad peccandum allicitur, & magis mediate per homines malos; propterea omnia haec tria partes inferi appellari possunt: nam per portam omnis potestas Satanae intelligenda est. Cum igitur Petrus ita in hanc Petram aedificandus erat, post resurrectionem Christi, ut nunquam deficeret, propterea audijt vocem illam, beatae consolationis plenissimam, [Simon, Simon &c.] {y}Beatus enim dictus est ex certitudine beatitudinis futurae per revelationem, nam Christus illi hac voce revelavit, quod ita habituras erat beatitudinem, ut iam de illa dubitare non poterat; & hoc fuit magnum donum. Haec Abulensis. Si vero [Porta Inferorum] nempe, potentia Satanae (vel per vitia alia, vel per Haresin) in Pontifices aliquos, ad æternam damnationem, vnquam præualuerint; per se consectarium erit, ex promissionibus istis, per Christum Petro factis, nullâ vi ingenij Ius aliquod Papale exprimi aut extorqueri posse.
units.tr: Christ said, [The gates of hell shall not prevail against it], that is, the Rock, as you say. Rightly so. Therefore not against Peter; yet this too, but not because Peter is himself the Rock and the foundation of the building (which honour is due to Christ alone), but because Peter is a stone built upon the Rock itself. And by [the gates of hell], as the Jesuit Maldonatus has very learnedly observed, {t}is understood simply, without any restriction, the whole power of the Devil; whether through heresies, as Epiphanius says; or through other vices, as Ambrose says; or through both, as Origen, Jerome and Bede say; or through the blasphemies of heretics, as Euthymius says; or through persecutions, as Theophylact says; or through seductive vices, as {u}Rabanus taught. Your Abulensis has set out the explanation of this clearly. {x}The gates are taken (he says) metaphorically, because one enters a house through a door; so that which leads to hell is called the gate of hell; and because a man is drawn to hell immediately through sin, but mediately through the passions by which he is enticed to sin, and still more mediately through evil men; therefore all these three can be called parts of hell, for by the gate is to be understood all the power of Satan. Since, then, Peter was to be built upon this Rock after the resurrection of Christ so that he would never fail, he therefore heard that voice, most full of blessed consolation, [Simon, Simon, etc.]. {y}He is called blessed from the certainty of future blessedness through revelation, for Christ revealed to him by that voice that he would have such blessedness that he could no longer doubt it; and this was a great gift. So Abulensis. But if [the gates of hell], that is, the power of Satan (whether through other vices or through heresy), had ever prevailed over some Pontiffs to eternal damnation, it would follow of itself that from those promises made by Christ to Peter no papal right can be drawn out or wrung by any power of wit.

units.la: Vtinam Pontificum, qui vt inter Mortales Sanctissimi, Beatissimiq; audire volunt, ea Sanctitas esset, vt dubitare nobis liceret, an quisquam eorum damnari vnquàm potuerit. Etiamsi enim Inquisitores pro fide Pontificiâ vbi verba hæc legerint, [ Papa peccans damnandus est vt Diabolus ] statim illa Deleri & expungi mandarint: non tamen puto Eos adeò stupendæ seu potiùs stupidæ fidei esse, vt credant quemlibet Pontificem necessariò salvatum iri. Vtinam potiùs non eo impietatis iamdiu deuenissent, vt, apud ipsos etiam Pontificios, non ambigendum sit, an fere quisquam Eorum saluari posset; {a}Quandoquidem (vt ait vester Maffonius) in Pontificibus nemo hodie Sanctitatem requirit, optimi putantur, si vel leuiter boni sint, vel minùs mali quàm cæteri mortales. Hoc Pontificiorum aliorum frequentes acerbæque querimoniæ declarant: Doletenim vehementiúsque deplorat Baronius, {b}Intrusos fuisse in Cathedram Petri homines monstrosos, vitâ turpissimos, moribusque perditissimos. Platina; {c}Licentiâ peccandi monstra, & portenta sedem Petri occupâsse. Genebrardus; {d}Per annos fere cl. Pontifices circiter l. à virtute maiorum deficientes, Apostaticos, Apostaticosq; potiùs quàm Apostolicos fuisse. Inter quos Bellarminus reperit {e}Iohannem XXIII. tam dissolutæ vitæ fuisse, vt vulgus existimaret eum negare vitam æternam. Quin-etiam, {f}Fieri posse, vt Pontifex Idola colat, --- & Diabolicis artibus operam nauet, Nè quidem Iesuitæ negabunt. Istiusmodi Pontifices tam monstra, támque mancipia Diaboli, fieri non potest, quin in portas Inferorum cum Diabolis ruant; quos fors eadem manet cum Pontifice illo, de quo Poëta Actius cecinit,
units.tr: Would that the holiness of the Pontiffs, who wish to be heard as the most holy and most blessed among mortals, were such that we might be allowed to doubt whether any of them could ever be damned. For even if the Inquisitors, when they read these words for the Papist faith, [A Pope who sins is to be damned like the Devil], at once ordered them to be erased and expunged, I do not think they are of such stupendous, or rather stupid, faith as to believe that any Pontiff whatever will necessarily be saved. Would that they had not long since fallen into such impiety that, even among the Papists themselves, there is no doubt whether almost any of them could be saved; {a}since (as your Maffonius says) today no one requires holiness in Pontiffs; they are thought excellent if they are even slightly good, or less bad than other mortals. The frequent and bitter complaints of other Papists declare this. For Baronius grieves and laments more keenly {b}that monstrous men, most vile in life and most corrupt in morals, were thrust into the chair of Peter. Platina: {c}monsters and portents, through licence to sin, occupied the see of Peter. Genebrardus: {d}over nearly 150 years about fifty Pontiffs, failing in the virtue of their forebears, were apostate, apostate rather than apostolic. Among whom Bellarmine finds {e}John XXIII to have been of so dissolute a life that the common people thought he denied eternal life. Moreover, {f}that a Pontiff may worship idols, --- and busy himself with diabolical arts, not even the Jesuits will deny. Pontiffs of this sort, such monsters and such slaves of the Devil, cannot fail to rush into the gates of hell along with the devils; and perhaps the same fate awaits them as that of the Pontiff of whom the poet Accius sang:

units.la: {g}Pollicitus cælum Romanus est astra Sacerdos, Per scelera, & cædes ad styga pandit iter. [?]
units.tr: {g}The Roman priest promises heaven and the stars; through crimes and slaughter he opens the way to the Styx. [?]

units.la: Cùm igitur ex promissionibus, quas Christus Simoni Petro dedit, constet, filium Dei ita pro eius fide, adeóque salute orâsse, vt non modò à fide non deficere, verum etiam itâ in poenitentiæ atque sanctitatis curriculo persisteret, vt Porta inferorum aduersus Eum non prævalerent (vndè est, quòd ab eius voce, qui & veritas & vita est, Beatus pronuncietur) certè hæc singularis felicitas in flagitiosissimos & sceleratissimos Pontifices deriuari nequit: quin potius, quod Simon Petrus in casu alio Simoni Mago dixit, id sibi Pontifices dictum putent; {h}Non est tibi fors, aut pars nobiscum in sermone isthoc. Hæc de improbitate Morum; sequitur de prauitate iudicij Pontificum, tam quoad privatam, quàm quoad publicam Personam.
units.tr: Since, then, it is evident from the promises which Christ gave to Simon Peter that the Son of God so prayed for his faith, and therefore for his salvation, that not only would he not fail in faith, but he would also persist in the course of repentance and holiness, so that the gates of hell would not prevail against him (which is why he is pronounced blessed by the voice of him who is both truth and life), surely this singular felicity cannot be derived to the most shameless and wicked Pontiffs. Rather, let them take to themselves what Simon Peter said in another case to Simon the Magician: {h}You have neither lot nor part with us in this matter. These remarks concern the wickedness of their morals; there follows the perversity of the Pontiffs' judgement, both as to their private and as to their public person.

units.la: III. ANIMADVERSIO.
units.tr: III. Animadversion.

units.la: Papam tum quà privatam personam; tum-etiam quà publicum Doctorem in hæresin incidere posse.
units.tr: That the Pope can fall into heresy both as a private person and as a public teacher.

units.la: Quoad privatam personam. Contra illud tuum [{*}Probabile, & pie credendum] Salmeron Iesuita multò Bellarmino antiquior (cui Valentinus, Costerus, & eiusdem Societatis alij plurimi assentiuntur) fatetur {i}Papam quemlibet, ut privatum, errare posse, & à fide deficere, etsi (inquit) noui Scriptores aliud defendere tentauerint, praeter communem Doctorum sensum. Imò etiam, quoad personam publicam, Eum hæreticum esse posse, hæresin aliquam pertinaciter docendo, difficile non esset ex vestris principijs demonstrare, si hoc esset huius loci. Satis nobis erit ostendere tales aliquos nonnunquàm extitisse. {k}Erasmus, in examinandis veterum scriptis, accuratissimi iudicij vir censoriâ notâ quasdam Pontificum contradictiones castigauit, in quibus aliquos Eorum errâsse necesse est, in Decretis, ad fidei negotium pertinentibus.
units.tr: As to his private person: against that claim of yours, [Probable, and to be piously believed], the Jesuit Salmeron, much older than Bellarmine (whom Valentia, Coster and many others of the same Society agree with), admits that {i}the Pope, as a private person, can err and fall away from the faith, even though (he says) newer writers have tried to defend otherwise, against the common sense of the teachers. Moreover, as to his public person, it would not be difficult to show from your own principles that he can be a heretic by stubbornly teaching some heresy, if this were the place for it. It will be enough for us to show that such men have sometimes existed. {k}Erasmus, a man of most accurate judgement in examining the writings of the ancients, censured with his critical mark certain contradictions of the Popes, in which some of them must have erred, in decrees that pertain to matters of faith.

units.la: Quis autem magis publicè pertinaciterque hæresin docuisse existimandus est, quàm Is, qui fuit eo nomine in orthodoxis Synodis publicè damnatus? Talis imprimis fuit (vt Alios taceam) Papa Honorius, qui purus putus Monothelitæ fuit; quæ nefaria hæresis in Christo duas voluntates, adeoque Christum θεάνθρωπον [?] esse negat. Etsi autem vix ulla Causa unquam aut pluribus aut antiquioribus, nobilioribusque testibus confirmata fuerit, quàm hæc de damnatione Honorij, surrexit tamen nudiustertius vnus Bellarminus, qui vt Honorij fidem tueretur, Authoribus istis omnem fidem derogandam censuerit. Respondet enim 1. {1}Deceptos fuisse Patres sextæ Synodi, qui Honorium damnârunt: quam tamen sententiam Legati Pontificy tolerabant. II. Deceptos septimæ Synodi Patres, qui sextæ Synodi sententiam confirmabant. III. Deceptum Adrianum sextum Papam, qui Honorium Hæreticum fuisse putabat. IV. Deceptum Leonem secundum Papam, qui Honorium Hæreticum execratus est. V. (quasi Bellarminus solus esset ἀνταγωνιστής [?]) Psellum, Thomam, & Epiphanium, aliosque omnes, qui Honorio hærefin tribuunt, deceptos fuisse: accidere enim posse, ait, ut Concilium generale erret in quæstione facti, non fidei. Quod effugium quàm sit miserum & deploratum nemo facilius Bellarmino suaserit, quàm ipsus Bellarminus. Vbi enim objicitur Illi à Protestantibus error Caipha summi Pont. Iudæorum in Concilio, à quo excommunicati erant, qui confitebantur Iesum Ioh. 11. Pontificijs alijs respondentibus, errâsse Caipham tantùm in quæstione de facto, non de iure [num Iesus necandus esset;] Responsum hoc tollit, {m}Nam quæstio illa (inquit) quamvis de facto esset, tamen involvebat quæstionem de fide gravissimam, nimirum, an Iesus esset verus Messias, & Dei filius, atque adeò Deus verus. Iccirco profecto non poterat quin, consimili prorsus ratione Sententia illa, quâ Papa Honorius Pontifex Rom. hæreseos damnatus est, Conclusionem inuolverit, nempe; Pontificem Romanum quatenus publicum Doctorem, Hæreticum esse posse, atque adeò à fide deficere: quâ Romanæ fidei (de infallibili Papæ iudicio) Articulus summus, & veluti Petra ipsa funditus euertitur.
units.tr: But who should be thought to have taught heresy more publicly and more stubbornly than the one who was publicly condemned for it by the orthodox Synods? Chief among such men (to say nothing of the others) was Pope Honorius, who was a plain and pure Monothelite. That impious heresy denies that there are two wills in Christ, and so denies that Christ is θεάνθρωπος [theanthropos]. Yet although scarcely any cause has ever been confirmed by more or older and more noble witnesses than this condemnation of Honorius, there has arisen, just the other day, one man, Bellarmine, who, in order to defend the faith of Honorius, has thought that all trust must be withdrawn from these authors. For he replies: 1. {1}The Fathers of the sixth Synod, who condemned Honorius, were deceived; yet the Papal legates tolerated this opinion. II. The Fathers of the seventh Synod, who confirmed the sentence of the sixth Synod, were deceived. III. Pope Adrian VI, who thought Honorius was a heretic, was deceived. IV. Pope Leo II, who execrated Honorius as a heretic, was deceived. V. (as if Bellarmine alone were the ἀνταγωνιστής [antagonist]) Psellus, Thomas, Epiphanius, and all the others who attribute heresy to Honorius were deceived; for it can happen, he says, that a general Council errs in a question of fact, not of faith. How wretched and hopeless this escape is, no one could more easily persuade Bellarmine than Bellarmine himself. For when the Protestants object to him the error of Caiaphas, the High Priest of the Jews, in the Council, from which those who confessed Jesus (John 11) had been excommunicated, and the other Papists reply that Caiaphas erred only in a question of fact, not of right [whether Jesus was to be put to death], this answer destroys itself. {m}For that question, he says, although it was about fact, nevertheless involved a most serious question of faith, namely, whether Jesus was the true Messiah and Son of God, and therefore truly God. Hence, in exactly the same way, that sentence by which Pope Honorius, Roman Pontiff, was condemned as a heretic necessarily involved this conclusion: that the Roman Pontiff, as a public teacher, can be a heretic, and so fall away from the faith. By this conclusion the highest article of the Roman faith (on the infallible judgement of the Pope) is utterly overturned, and as it were the very rock is undermined.

units.la: Quod autem Iesuitæ alij respondent, errâsse Eum; vt priuatum Doctorem; at, ut Pontificem, veritatem prædicasse: hoc, nisi ad pudorem illis incutiendum, nihil valet; tùm quia Honorius à Concilio non ut priuatus Doctor, sed ut Pontifex iudicatus & damnatus est: tùm quòd (fatente Bellarmino) hominem in se {n}Haereticum contrarium fidem prædicare, violentum est, & non secundum providentiam Dei omnia suauiter disponentis; quod non magis à Pontifice Haeretico expectandum autumat, quàm ut Asinus ratiocinetur: tum etiam quia, ut erudite admodum Episcopus vester (aduersus Eos, qui respondebant Gregorium primum perperam iudicasse, sed ut virum sapientem, non ut Pontificem) {o}Persona, inquit, eadem est numero Gregorius, ut Papa, & ut non Papa (seu priuatus Doctor) & idò æqualis sapientiæ, sed non æqualis potestatis; quia Papatus potestatem addit, potestas autem est ad aliquid iubendum vel statuendum, sed non ad aliquid veriùs dicendum.
units.tr: As for the other Jesuits who reply that he erred as a private teacher but preached the truth as Pope, this answer is worth nothing, unless it is meant to shame them. First, because Honorius was judged and condemned by the Council not as a private teacher but as a Pope. Second, because (as Bellarmine himself admits) {n}for a heretic to preach a doctrine contrary to the faith is violent, and not in accordance with the providence of God, who disposes all things sweetly; which he says we should no more expect from a heretical Pope than that an ass would reason. Third, because, as your bishop has very learnedly argued against those who replied that Gregory I judged wrongly, but as a wise man, not as Pope: {o}The person of Gregory, he says, is numerically the same whether as Pope or as not Pope (that is, as a private teacher), and so equal in wisdom, but not equal in power; because the papacy adds power, and power is for commanding or decreeing something, not for saying something more truly.

units.la: Quod hic de Gregorio, idem ego vobis de Honorio responsum subijcio, nempè; Pontificis personam publicam ad aliquid magis publicè decernendum valere posse; sed non ad aliquid magis verè & Orthodoxè sentiendum & definiendum. Quidni igitur, contra Bellarminum, multò sanè apertioris pectoris Authorem vestrum opponam, asserentem {p}Honorium Pont. (Addo ego, ut Pontificem) non posse ab errore vindicari, quem (inquit) Pfellus, Thomasius, Theodorus, Epiphanius, Beda, tota denique septima Synodus, Adrianus quoque, Agatho, & Leo (Tres Pontifices Rom.) Haereticum esse iudicabant? Miraberis igitur proculdubiò, Lector, quà fide, quàue conscientiâ Bellarminus Principes Germanos in reprobum sensum datos dixerit, tantùm, quòd sententiam suam, de infallibili Papæ iudicio, damnârunt; quam tantâ nube omne genus Testium, Historicorum, Theologorum, Pontificum, Conciliorum; & (quod etiam maximi momenti est) ipsorum Causæ huius Propugnatorum repugnantijs labefactatum, & protritum uiderit. Sed, Magna est veritas, & praualebit. Hæc de Pontificis fide, sequitur de Sede.
units.tr: What is said here of Gregory I, I answer for you about Honorius in the same way: the public person of the Pope can avail for deciding something more publicly, but not for thinking and defining something more truly and orthodoxly. Why then should I not, against Bellarmine, set against him your author, who was of a much more open heart, asserting {p}that Pope Honorius (I add, as Pope) cannot be cleared of the error which (he says) Psellus, Thomas, Theodore, Epiphanius, Bede, the whole seventh Synod, Adrian too, Agatho, and Leo (three Roman Pontiffs) judged to be heresy? You will be astonished, reader, by what faith or conscience Bellarmine called the German princes given over to a reprobate mind, merely because they condemned his opinion on the infallible judgement of the Pope; an opinion which he has seen overwhelmed and worn down by such a cloud of every kind of witness: historians, theologians, Popes, Councils; and (which is also of the greatest weight) by the contradictions of the very defenders of this cause. But great is the truth, and it will prevail. So much for the faith of the Pope; now follows his see.

units.la: Bellarminus de Offic.
units.tr: Bellarmine, On the Office.

units.la: “ Et illam Ecclesiam requisiste (Principes) de qua dictum est a Domino, [Portae inferi non praevalebunt adversus eam.] --pag.31.
units.tr: "And they sought out that Church of which the Lord said, [The gates of hell shall not prevail against it]." --p. 31.

units.la: Explicatio.
units.tr: Explanation.

units.la: {c}Quam Tu Ecclesiam intelligis? {1}Ostendimus (inquis, sed alibi) Petra, & fundamentum Ecclesiae dicitur Petrus, ut summus Rector Ecclesiae, & proinde quilibet eius Successor est similiter Petra. {r}Secunda propositio est, non solum Pontifex Rom. non potest errare in fide, sed neque Romana particularis Ecclesia; {f}perstiente Romae Sede Apostolica.
units.tr: Which Church do you mean? "We have shown (you say, but elsewhere) that Peter is called the rock and foundation of the Church, as its supreme ruler, and therefore every one of his successors is likewise a rock." "The second proposition is that not only can the Roman Pontiff not err in faith, but neither can the particular Roman Church, so long as the Apostolic See remains at Rome."

units.la: I. ANIMADVERSIO.
units.tr: I. Animadversion.

units.la: Catholicam Ecclesiam Romanae Sedi non ita esse affixam, ut non Roma ipsa possit esse Babylon Apocalyp- tica.
units.tr: The Catholic Church is not so bound to the Roman See that Rome itself cannot be the Apocalyptic Babylon.

units.la: {*}TRia obicis; Petrum, Papam Romanum, & Romanam Ecclesiam. De singulis supra pluribus disceptavimus, quorum quidem iusta ac plena tractatio taedium & fastidium Lectori crearet: Ad summa igitur haec capita digitum duntaxat intendam. Primum erat Petrum non esse ipsam Petram, sed Christum. Secundum, Papam non esse Petrum, nedum Petram; quippe in peccatorum gurgite demersus plerumque non potest esse Petrus, de quo Christus, [Tu conversus &c.] Deinde quum Papa, quoad privatam personam, tam per infidelitatem, quam per impotentiam possit damnari, non potest esse Petrus, de quo Christus tum pronunciavit, [Beatus es Simon &c.] Porro quia Papa, quoad publicam suam personam, qua Papa, posit esse Haereticus, & haereses definire atque defendere; non potest esse Petrus, pro quo Christus [rogavit, ne fides eius deficeret.] Tertium; Ecclesiam Rom. haud posse censeri illam Catholicam Matrem, extra quam nulla est salus; nisi, ad hoc portentosum dogma asserendum stabiliendumque, plurimas * Ecclesias florentissimas vetustioris iuxta & posterioris aetatis; nisi antiquos Patres, omnium iudicio, celeberrimos ac Catholicissimos; nisi sanctissimos, gloriosissimosque Christi Martyres velimus ex Saluandorum albo, coetuque expungere. Quae omnia ex Pontificiorum multorum testimoniis locupletissimis Nos supra probauimus.
units.tr: You raise three points: Peter, the Roman Pope, and the Roman Church. I have disputed each of these above at length, though a full treatment would bore and weary the reader, so I will touch only on the main heads. The first was that Peter is not the rock itself, but Christ. The second, that the Pope is not Peter, let alone the rock; for one sunk in the whirlpool of sins often cannot be Peter, of whom Christ said, [When you have turned again, etc.]. Then, since the Pope, as a private person, can be damned both through unbelief and through incapacity, he cannot be Peter, of whom Christ then pronounced [Blessed are you, Simon, etc.]. Further, since the Pope, as a public person, as Pope, can be a heretic and can define and defend heresies, he cannot be Peter, for whom Christ [prayed that his faith should not fail]. The third: the Roman Church cannot be regarded as that Catholic Mother, outside of whom there is no salvation; unless, to assert and establish this monstrous dogma, we are willing to strike from the roll of the saved very many flourishing churches of both older and later times; unless we are willing to strike the ancient Fathers, by everyone's judgment the most famous and most Catholic, and the most holy and glorious martyrs of Christ, from the list and company of the saved. All these things we have proved above from the very rich testimonies of many Papists.

units.la: Veruntamen, quàm Pontificij nullis praestigijs facilius credulis hominibus, & parum cautis fucum faciant, quàm iactando se esse Rom. Ecclesiae filios; hancque solam Sedem esse Petri, quam Christus salutifera voce suâ beauit, quando pronunciabat, [Ecclesiam ædificatam esse supra petram, aduersus quam portae inferorum nunquam praeualebunt :] operae fortassis pretium erit hanc laruam Aduersarijs detrahere; eoque magis, quia nihil Illis potius, nihil antiquius est, quàm de hac Romanae Sedis praerogatiuâ insolenter, & Thrasonicè gloriari. Sic enim Cardinalis Baronius ; {t}Roma, quum coleret Idola, iure dicta est Babylonia; postea vero, ob sacrae religionis cultum, in Dei ciuitatem conuersa, non amplius Babylon pagano nomine appellata : Vnde Arnulphus Comes, scriptor fidelissimus, Hinc (inquit) ciuitatem intuentes, affirmant verba sacrae Scripturae Psal. 16. Omnipotens Roma, gloriosa dicta sunt de te; quia ciuitas Dei es facta. Vespertilio ad Solem es, (Baronii) in tenebris cernis nescio quid, in clarissima luce penitus coecutis. Scripturae verba arripis tàm à Roma aliena, quàm Hierosolymis propria. At quae in libro Reuelationis de Roma propriè perspicuéque reuelata sunt, Apoc. 18. [{u}Cecidit Babylon illa magna : cum qua Reges terrae scortati sunt ; Exite ex eâ :] ea non sumi historicè, vt Tu vis, de Roma Ethnica, quae multis retro seculis extincta est, sed Propheticè de Roma amplius futurâ, duo Iesuitae insignioris notae diserte luculenterq; demonstrant. Vnus est Ribera; {x}Babylon est Roma, vt adhuc sutura est &c. — Qui diminare me dixerit, ego ore vt praiudicium deponat, remq; totam maturo iudicio examinet, nec plus mihi credat, quam veritas persuaserit. Hæc Ille. Alter est Viegas; {a}Hoc (inquit) manifestum est ex textu &c. Qui plura cupit, Authores ipsos consulat.
units.tr: Yet how easily the Papists, by boasting that they are sons of the Roman Church, and that this alone is the See of Peter whom Christ blessed with his saving voice when he said, [the Church is built upon the rock, against which the gates of hell shall never prevail], deceive credulous people and those who are not cautious, with no tricks at all: perhaps it will be worth the trouble to strip this mask from our opponents. All the more so because nothing is dearer or more important to them than to boast insolently and boastfully of this prerogative of the Roman See. For Cardinal Baronius says: Rome, while it worshipped idols, was rightly called Babylon; afterwards, however, turned into the city of God through the worship of the sacred religion, it is no longer called Babylon by a pagan name. Hence Arnulphus Comes, a most faithful writer: Looking upon the city from here, they affirm that the words of holy Scripture, Psalm 16, "Glorious things are spoken of you, O Rome, Almighty," are said of you, because you have become the city of God. You are a bat before the sun, Baronius: in the dark you see I know not what, and in the clearest light you are wholly blinded. You snatch at words of Scripture that are as foreign to Rome as they are proper to Jerusalem. But what is revealed plainly and clearly about Rome in the book of Revelation, Rev. 18, [Babylon the great has fallen, with whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication; come out of her], is not to be taken historically, as you wish, of pagan Rome, which was extinct many centuries ago, but prophetically, of a Rome yet to come. Two Jesuits of notable repute demonstrate this clearly and lucidly. One is Ribera: Babylon is Rome, as it is yet to be, etc. If anyone says I am belittling him, I beg him to put aside prejudice and examine the whole matter with mature judgment, and not believe me any more than the truth persuades him. Thus he. The other is Viegas: This is manifest, he says, from the text, etc. Whoever wants more should consult the authors themselves.

units.la: Ad Card. Baronium reuertor. {b}Eulogium Doctoris gentium (inquit) verax iugiter perseueret, [Rom.1.fides vestra annunciatur in toto mundo.] Tolleti Cardinalis Responsum huius interpretamenti vanitatem facilè ostendet, qui obseruat eundem Apostolum de Thessalonicensibus idem tulisse Eulogium. 1.Thess.1. In omni loco fides vestra, quæ est in Deum, profecta est. Et paulò post, vbi Apostolus, [Proposui venire ad vos (Romanos) vt aliquem fructum habeam in vobis, sicut in cæteris gentibus.] {c}Perpende (inquit Toletus) Euangelij indifferentiam; quamuis enim Romani inter cæteras Gentes eminerent, & primatum (intelligit politicum) haberent, tamen in prædicatione Euangelij, & salutis negotio pares eos facit; [In vobis, inquit, sicut in cæteris gentibus:] non enim apud Deum, est distinctio Iudæi, Græci, Romani, nationum, aut conditionum hominum. Hæc Toletus Iesuita; quo tota vestra Societas non peperit Expositorem saniorem, aut candidiorem: cuius testimonio non video quid magis facere possit ad reprimendam istam vestram, de Rom. Ecclesiæ prærogatiua, vanam, & præcipitem arrogantiam.
units.tr: I return to Cardinal Baronius. "The praise of the Teacher of the Gentiles (he says) continues ever true: [Rom. 1, 'your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world']." Toletus's answer to this interpretation will easily show its emptiness; he observes that the same Apostle bestowed the same praise on the Thessalonians: 1 Thess. 1, "In every place your faith toward God has gone forth." And a little later, where the Apostle says, [I purposed to come to you (Romans), that I might have some fruit among you, as among the other Gentiles]. "Consider (says Toletus) the impartiality of the Gospel. For although the Romans stood out among the other nations and held primacy (he means political primacy), yet in the preaching of the Gospel and in the business of salvation he makes them equal. [Among you, he says, as among the other nations]: for with God there is no distinction of Jew, Greek, Roman, of nations or of conditions of men." Thus Toletus the Jesuit, than whom your whole Society has produced no saner or fairer expositor. By his testimony I do not see what could do more to check your vain and headlong arrogance concerning the prerogative of the Roman Church.

units.la: At Romanam eam esse Ecclesiam Catholicâ, quam in Symbolo credimus, & de quâ extat promissio Christi, [{d}Portas Inferorum non prævalituras aduersus eam] Bellarminus dictitat : quale Interpretamentum antiquorum {*}Patrum nemo concepit vnquàm, nè per somnium quidem.
units.tr: But Bellarmine keeps insisting that the Roman Church is that Catholic Church which we believe in the Creed, and of which Christ made the promise, [that the gates of hell shall not prevail against it]. No one of the ancient Fathers ever conceived such an interpretation, not even in a dream.

units.la: Inter Pontificios Caietanus, & Ferus intelligunt non communiter acceptam Congregationem Eorum, qui {e}Christiani dicuntur, siue boni sunt, siue mali, — sed Ecclesiam secundum Spiritum, nempe Electorum; {*}qui eádem fide, spe, charitate præditi sunt. Atque hunc sensum sacræ Scripturæ nobis præbent plerique omnes Theologi, vbicunque de Catholica (id est, vniuersaliter sumptâ) Ecclesia tractant.
units.tr: Among the Papists, Cajetan and Ferus understand by the Church not the commonly accepted congregation of those who are called Christians, whether good or bad, but the Church according to the Spirit, namely of the elect, who are endowed with the same faith, hope and charity. Most theologians also give us this sense of Holy Scripture wherever they treat of the Catholic (that is, universally taken) Church.

units.la: Brevitatis ergò, Causæ huius Episcopum vestrum Abulensem feremus Judicem. {f}Non est verum (inquit) quod supra Petrum ædificata est Ecclesia, quia solus Christus est fundamentum Ecclesiæ: & patet, quia necesse est vt fundamentum Ecclesiæ sit immortale. At de Successoribus Petri patet, quod multi eorum, etiam Canonicè intrantes, prolapsi sunt in hæresin, & alij in cultum Idolorum: ---- atque ità, Papâ deficiente, tota interiret Ecclesia. Et Ecclesia in hoc loco non sicut communiter accepta, sed solos electos complectitur. Hæc ille. Eant igitur Adversarij nostri, & Jactitent, ex suo Bozio, Papam universorum Episcoporum in Ecclesiapersonam sustinere; ex Baronio glorientur, Romam esse civitatem Dei gloriosam; cuius fides jugiter per totum orbem annunciatur: ex Bellarmino triumphent, Papam Romæ esse Ecclesiæ Petram; & Ecclesiam Romanam eam esse, contra quam portæ Inferi non prævalebunt: Atque ideo in Principes Germanos constrepant, tanquàm in homines datos in reprobum sensum; quod nimirum eo stupiditatis se adigi atque pertrahi non sinunt, ut credant Ecclesiam eam, cuius tanquàm immediatum fundamentum Papa est, qui (juxta confessionem penè universorum) Hereticus esse possit, in Petram ædificari, & non potius planè in arenam. Hactenùs de Tertio Titulo Papæ, nimirùm, Doctoris, & Judicis Christianorum.
units.tr: For brevity's sake, let us take your Abulensis, the Bishop of Ávila, as judge of this cause. It is not true (he says) that the Church is built upon Peter, because Christ alone is the foundation of the Church; and it is clear, because the foundation of the Church must necessarily be immortal. But it is clear of the successors of Peter that many of them, even those who entered canonically, have fallen into heresy, and others into the worship of idols: and so, if the Pope fails, the whole Church would perish. And in this place the Church is not taken as commonly understood, but embraces only the elect. Thus he. Let our opponents therefore go and boast, from their Bozio, that the Pope sustains the person of all bishops in the Church; let them glory from Baronius that Rome is the glorious city of God, whose faith is continually proclaimed throughout the whole world; let them triumph from Bellarmine that the Pope is the Rock of the Church at Rome, and the Roman Church is that against which the gates of hell shall not prevail. And let them clamour against the German princes, as men given over to a reprobate mind, because forsooth they do not allow themselves to be driven and drawn into such stupidity as to believe that the Church, of which the Pope is the immediate foundation, and who (by the confession of almost everyone) can be a heretic, is built upon a rock, rather than wholly upon sand. So far concerning the third title of the Pope, namely, of Teacher and Judge of Christians.

units.la: CAP. IIII. DE QVARTO TITVLO PAPAE, VIDELICET, SPECVLATOR.
units.tr: CHAP. IIII. ON THE FOURTH TITLE OF THE POPE, NAMELY, WATCHMAN (SPECULATOR).

units.la: “Quartum nomen Pontificis Speculator est; ipse enim prop-tereà in altissimo fastigio sedet specula Pastoralis, ut S. Augustinus loquitur in principio quatuor librorum ad Bonifacium Papam. ---- Pag.31.
units.tr: "The fourth name of the Pontiff is Speculator; for he therefore sits on the highest summit of the Pastoral watch-tower, as St Augustine says at the beginning of the four books to Pope Boniface." ---- Page 31.

units.la: I. ANIMADVERSIO.
units.tr: I. ANIMADVERSION.

units.la: Augustinum Bonifacio Papae fastigium concessisse, fastum adimisse.
units.tr: That Augustine granted Pope Boniface a lofty position, but took away his arrogance.

units.la: DUm Roma adhuc metropolis, & quasi emporium erat orbis Christiani, non difficile fuit Augustino in ea Pastoralis specula fastigium altissimum intueri; quando nimirum, propter loci amplitudinem, Papae, non quidem Super alios, sed tamen Præ alijs effulgebat authoritas. Exemplum nobis luculentum erit (nè longius repetamus) idem Bonifacius, qui, in causa {*}Appellationis, Speculæ suæ fastigium paulò altius erigens, quàm par erat, ab Africanis Patribus (inter quos Augustinus pars magna fuit) ab isthoc culmine, non sine ignominia, deiectus penitus obmutuit. Quodsi Africani Bonifacij II. coeteroquin Viri sancti (vt Vos censetis) prærogatiuam, tanquàm Typhum (sic enim appellabant) repulerint; quantis, obsecro, sannis Bonifacium VIII. excepissent, præ cuius superbia, vel insania potius, Illius Typhus modestia videretur? quùm nimirùm hic supra summos Monarchas, etiam in Temporalibus, Speculæ suæ fastigium attolleret: De quo *supra. Tu perge, & Speculationis officium expone.
units.tr: While Rome was still the metropolis and, as it were, the marketplace of the Christian world, it was not difficult for Augustine to see in it the highest summit of the pastoral watch-tower; since, on account of the greatness of the city, the authority of the Pope shone forth, not indeed above others, but before others. A clear example (lest we go on too long) will be the same Boniface, who, in the cause of appeal, raised the summit of his watch-tower somewhat higher than was fitting, and was cast down from that peak by the African Fathers (among whom Augustine was a leading figure), not without disgrace, and fell utterly silent. But if the Africans rejected the prerogative of Boniface II, otherwise a holy man (as you think), as Typhus (for so they called it), with what mockery, I beg you, would they have received Boniface VIII, before whose pride, or rather madness, the modesty of that Typhus would seem...? For he indeed raised the summit of his watch-tower above the greatest monarchs, even in temporal matters, as was said above. Go on, then, and expound the duty of watching.

units.la: Bellarminus de Offic.
units.tr: Bellarminus de Offic.

units.la: “ Quoniam ad Illum pertinet speculari ex alto quid agant Christiani, & inde malos admonet, vt redeant in viam; & bonos hortetur, vt perseuerent in cursu, & perueniant ad Brauium. — Pag.31.32.
units.tr: "Since it belongs to him to watch from on high what Christians are doing, and from there to warn the wicked to return to the way, and to exhort the good to persevere in the course and reach the prize." ---- Pages 31, 32.

units.la: I. ANIMADVERSIO.
units.tr: I. ANIMADVERSION.

units.la: Speculandi officium, Episcopis omnibus æquè impositum, nullam esse Papalis Dominationis argumentum.
units.tr: The duty of watching, imposed equally on all bishops, is no proof of papal dominion.

units.la: QVid nobis hic Pontifici tuo peculiare occurrit? quid non etiam cuiuis legitimo Episcopo commune? hanc enim Speculam aliis Episcopis omnibus communem esse, vel hoc nomen Episcopus, ex communi Ethnicorum, nedùm Christianorum, vsu satis ostendit.
units.tr: What is there here that is peculiar to your Pontiff? What is not common to every lawful bishop? For that this watch-tower is common to all other bishops is sufficiently shown by the very name bishop, from the common usage not only of Christians but even of the heathens.

units.la: I. Apud Ethnicos. {a}Episcopi nomen (ait Balbus) à vetustis temporibus deductum: nam Athenienses quos speculatum mittebant, quid ni unusquisque Subditorum civitate boni maluè ageretur, Eos Episcopos, id est, Speculatores vocabant; ut apud Plutarchum Scipio Africanus Episcopus gentium; & Cicero ad Atticum Episcopus in oris maritimis dicebatur. Nec multò aliter {b}Onuphrius. Atque hanc Speculationem ex Alto faciendam esse, plurimae in Scripturis metaphoræ denotant. Vox enim prædicantis Alta esse debet; {c}Iohannes erat vox clamantis: Exemplum eius in Alto; {d}Lucerna non sub modio, sed in candelabro posita: Locus in Alto, nimirùm, in celeberrimo hominum concentu; {e}Quicquid didicisti in aure prædicate super tectum. Nihil nisi Altũ & excelsum Episcopos decet, unum dũtaxat si caueant, nè ex alto & elato corde aliorũ Christianorum mores Speculentur, & despiciant, {f}Discite à me (ait Christus) quia humilis Ego, & mitis. Nullam adhuc video in hoc officio Speculandi Pontificiæ eminentiæ nè umbram quidem. Hanc forsan ex verbis tuis proximis accipiemus.
units.tr: I. Among the heathens. {a}The name bishop (says Balbus) is derived from ancient times: for the Athenians, whom they sent as watchmen, so that the affairs of the state might be better managed, they called bishops, that is, watchmen; as in Plutarch Scipio Africanus was called bishop of the nations, and Cicero in his letter to Atticus was called bishop of the maritime shores. Onuphrius writes in much the same way. {b}That this watching is to be done from on high, many metaphors in the Scriptures indicate. For the voice of the preacher ought to be on high: {c}John was "the voice of one crying." Example of this on high: {d}"a lamp is not put under a bushel, but on a lampstand." A place on high, namely, in the most crowded gathering of men: {e}"What you have heard in the ear, preach upon the housetops." Nothing but what is lofty and high befits bishops, provided only they take care lest they spy out and despise the morals of other Christians from a high and proud heart: {f}"Learn from me" (says Christ), "for I am humble and meek." I see, in this office of watching, not even a shadow of Papal eminence as yet. Perhaps we shall gather it from your next words.

units.la: Bellarminus de Offic.
units.tr: Bellarminus de Offic.

units.la: Huius Speculatoris figura fuit propheta Hieremias, S. Bernardo teste, sic enim loquitur Deus ad Hieremiam, [ * Ecce constitui te hodiè super gentes, & super regna, ut evellas, & destruas, & disperdas, & dissipes, & ædifices, & plantes; neque significant hæc verba mandari à Deo, ut bella gerat cum regnis & Regibus, & ea sibi armis subjiciat; sed ut in Alto sedens observet malos mores, & corruptelas omnium Regum & regnorum, & clamando & vociferando liberrimè increpet vitia, præsertim publica, & Regum, & Principum, & populorum: & pœnas à Deo paratas prædicat, & ipse quoque Censuris, pœnisq; aliis coërceat contumaces, & eo modo dispergat, & destruat peccata Regum & populorum, & ædificet & plantet virtutes, ac bonos mores. — Pag.32.
units.tr: "The figure of this watchman was the prophet Jeremiah, as St Bernard bears witness; for thus God speaks to Jeremiah: [Behold, I have set you this day over the nations and over the kingdoms, to pluck up and to break down, to destroy and to scatter, to build and to plant]. These words do not signify that God commands him to wage war on kingdoms and kings and subdue them by arms; but that, sitting on high, he should observe the evil morals and corruptions of all kings and kingdoms, and with crying out and vociferation freely rebuke vices, especially public ones, both of kings and princes and of peoples; and proclaim the punishments prepared by God; and he himself should also restrain the obstinate by censures and other penalties, and in that way scatter and destroy the sins of kings and peoples, and build up and plant virtues and good morals." ---- Page 32.

units.la: I. ANIMADVERSIO.
units.tr: I. ANIMADVERSION.

units.la: Pontifices, ad suam Tyrannidem stabiliendam, Scripturam hanc [Hier.1.] egregiè peruertere; idq; ex Bernardi, Bellarmini, aliorumq; Antithesi demonstrari.
units.tr: The Pontiffs, in order to establish their tyranny, pervert this Scripture [Jer. 1.] most egregiously; and this is shown by the contrast with Bernard, Bellarmine and others.

units.la: GRegorius VII.Papa apud se statuit {f}Philippum, (Henrici filium) Francorum Regem excommunicare, & alium quemuis, qui ei Regalem honorem, aut obedientiam exhiberet. Hoc Gregorij propositum commemorans, vehementer exultat Baronius, Eúmque dicit, {g}Ad correptionem Regum, & purgationem Ecclesiæ à Deo positum — instar Hieremiæ, cui dixit, Constitui te hodiè super gentes, & super Regna, ut euellas &c. Deinde Romani Pontificis operâ (ut vos iactitatis) Imperatoribus Constantinopolitanis magna Imperij pars abrepta est; Henricus, & Fredericus Impp. Regnis priuati: ut hanc Pontificum authoritatem {h}Sanderus firmer, ad eandem figuram recurrit; Dominus(inquit) ad Hieremiam Sacerdotem in figura Christi dixit, Ecce constitui Te super Gentes, & Regna, ut euellas &c. Paulus III. Papa Principibus, & Ducibus Angliae, coeterisque Nobilibus praecepit, ut vi & armis Henrico VIII. Angliae Regi se opponerent, Illúmque è Regni finibus eijcere niterentur: formáque Pontificis Bulle ita se habet; {i}Paulus Episcopus Seruus seruorum Dei &c. — Nos in iustitia sede constituti, iuxta Prophetae vaticinium, dicentis, Ecce constitui te super Gentes, & Regna, ut euellas, & destruas. Eodem tenore usus est Pius V. Papa[?] aduersus omnium Reginarum, quae sunt, quae [illegible, ~6 letters] Phoenicem, ELIZABETHAM Angliae Reginam, in Bulla, qua Eam, subditis à fidelitatis suae iuramentis absolutis, regimine omni exauctorauit. {k}Pius &c. — Regnans in excelsis, cui data omnis in coelo & in terra potestas, quem super Gentes, & super omnia Regna Principem constituit, quicuellat[?], destruat &c. Undè est quòd Baronius, Sanderus, aliàque Papae mancipia de hac Scriptura tantopere insultent; inter quos Carerius (ut Papae potestatem temporalem super Reges confirmet:) {l}Hoc (inquit) Propheta Hieremias in persona Christi ad Romanum Pontificem loquitur; [Ecce constitui te super Gentes & Regna;] scilicet, per correctionem, & punitionem, si Reges mali fuerint. Haec Illi.
units.tr: Gregory VII, the Pope, resolved to excommunicate Philip, son of Henry, King of the French, and any other who should show him royal honour or obedience. Recalling this purpose of Gregory, Baronius exults greatly and calls him one "placed by God for the correction of kings and the purging of the Church," like Jeremiah, to whom it was said, "I have set you this day over nations and over kingdoms, to pluck up," etc. Then, by the work of the Roman Pontiff (as you boast), a great part of the empire was snatched from the Constantinopolitan emperors; the emperors Henry and Frederick were deprived of their kingdoms. Sanders, to confirm this authority of the Pontiffs, has recourse to the same figure: "The Lord," he says, "said to Jeremiah the priest, in the figure of Christ, Behold, I have set you over nations and kingdoms, to pluck up," etc. Pope Paul III ordered the princes and dukes of England and the other nobles to oppose King Henry VIII of England with force and arms, and to strive to drive him out of the borders of the kingdom; and the form of the Pope's bull runs thus: "Paul, bishop, servant of the servants of God, etc. — We, placed in the seat of justice, according to the prophecy of the prophet saying, Behold, I have set you over nations and kingdoms, to pluck up and to destroy." In the same tenor Pius V used against Elizabeth, Queen of England, the Phoenix of all the queens who are [illegible], in the bull by which, having absolved the subjects from their oaths of allegiance, he deprived her of all rule. "Pius, etc. — Reigning on high, to whom all power in heaven and on earth is given, whom he has set as prince over the nations and over all kingdoms, who plucks up, destroys, etc." Hence it is that Baronius, Sanders and other slaves of the Pope insult so greatly over this Scripture; among whom Carerius (in order to confirm the papal temporal power over kings) says: "This the prophet Jeremiah speaks in the person of Christ to the Roman Pontiff: [Behold, I have set you over nations and kingdoms]; namely, for correction and punishment, if kings are evil." So he.

units.la: In Titulo superiore Bellarminus Pontificem Rom. Omnium Christianorum Doctorem, & Iudicem supremum nobis violenter obtrusit; Cuius Decreta publica, quae ad fidem spectent, pro indubitatis Dei oraculis habeantur: hoc in loco Pontifices (quam praecipuam fidei suae columnam Pontificij habent) ex ipso verbo fidei Prophetae Hieremiae figuram proferunt, ad Authoritatem suam in Principes stabiliendam: ex quâ, tanquam ex Armamentario, nihil aliud, quàm sicas,hastas,gladios,omniáque instrumenta bellica depromunt, quibus omnium aduersantium Principum regna non quidem figuratè & metaphoricè, sed verè & [illegible, ~8 letters] authoritate sua Euellant, destruant, dissipent, atque disperdant: Atque hunc esse Scripturæ sensum in Bullis suis proclamant, & profitentur; quibus nihil ab ijs magis publicè exprimi & decerni aut soleat, aut possit. At en! verbi diuini insignes deprauatores, & deliros atq; mendaces Iudices vestros Rom. Pontifices. Ecquis omnium, inquies, ex Pontificiorum grege id ausus est dicere? Non nemo; ipsus, inquam, Bellarminus : "Non significant (inquit) verba Prophetæ, vt bella gerat cum Regibus, aut eos armis subjiciat; sed vt mores obseruet, vitia increpet, & poenas à Deo paratas prædicat. Quo vero teste? Bernardo (inquit) lib. 2. de considerat. ad Eugenium IV. Papam.
units.tr: In the title above, Bellarmine violently forced upon us the Roman Pontiff as teacher and supreme judge of all Christians, whose public decrees concerning faith are to be held as indubitable oracles of God. In this place the Pontiffs (which the Papists have as their chief pillar of faith) bring forward, from the very word of faith, the figure of the prophet Jeremiah, to establish their authority over princes; and from it, as from an armoury, they draw out nothing but daggers, spears, swords and all instruments of war, with which they would uproot, destroy, scatter and utterly ruin the kingdoms of all opposing princes, not indeed figuratively and metaphorically, but truly and by their own authority. And they proclaim and profess in their Bulls that this is the sense of Scripture, than which nothing is or can be more publicly expressed and decreed by them. But lo! notable corrupters of the divine word, and mad and lying judges, are your Roman Pontiffs. Who of the whole flock of the Papists, you will ask, has dared to say this? Not a few; Bellarmine himself, I say: "These words of the prophet do not signify (he says) that he should wage war with kings or subdue them by arms; but that he should observe their morals, rebuke their vices, and proclaim the punishments prepared by God." And on whose testimony? "Bernard (he says), book 2 On Consideration, to Pope Eugenius IV." He does this rightly in citing so weighty a witness; but if he had explained that testimony more clearly, he would have done much better, for thus Bernard speaks to Pope Eugenius. {m}"God says to the prophet, that you may pluck up and destroy, etc." What in these words sounds of pride?

units.la: Qui, quòd tàm grauem testem citat, rectè hoc quidem; quod si verò testimonium eius clarius explicâsset, multò fecisset rectius: sic enim ad Papam Eugenium Bernardus. {m}Dicit Deus Prophetæ, vt euellas, & destruas &c. Quid horum fastum sonat? schemate quodam magis rusticani sudoris labor (spiritualis expressus est), vt nos sentiamus impositum esse nobis ministerium, non dominium datum. Esto Propheta, sed nunquid plusquàm Propheta? si sapis, eris contentus mensurâ, quàm mensus est Dominus, quod amplius est ex malo est. Papa, & S. Bernardus vterque sacras Scripturas delibant, sed vah quàm dispari palato? Papa enim; Ergo hoc mihi dictum est in persona Christi. Bern. Nequaquàm, sed vt Nos sentiamus impositum esse nobis ministerium: Ergo, non magis quàm mihi. Papa; Ergo, Bella excitabo. At (Expositore vel Bellarmino) Non, vt Propheta bella gerat. Papa; Ergo in excelsis Ego regnans supra Reges, &c. Bern. Imo Ministerium verba sonant, non Dominium. Papa: Ergo, Regna ab alijs auferam, in alios conferam, vt Regum Dominus, quia figuram in Propheta habeo. Bern. Falleris, non Imperatorij & politici, sed spirispiritualis, & quasi rusticani laboris Schema hoc est; nec tu plusquam Propheta. Papa; Ergo tamen hoc faciam, quia est in ordine ad Deum, & ad bonum confert spirituale. Bern. Si sapis eris contentus mensura tua, quod enim amplius est ex malo est.
units.tr: Here he rightly cites so weighty a witness, but if he had explained the testimony more clearly he would have done much better. For Bernard speaks thus to Pope Eugenius: God says to the Prophet, that you should pluck up and destroy, etc. What does this sound of pride? The labour is expressed through a figure of speech, as of rustic sweat (spiritual), so that we may understand a ministry to have been laid upon us, not a lordship given. Be a Prophet, but are you more than a Prophet? If you are wise, you will be content with the measure the Lord has measured out, for whatever is more than that is of evil. The Pope and St Bernard both taste the sacred Scriptures, but oh, with how different a palate! For the Pope says: Therefore this was said to me in the person of Christ. Bernard: By no means, but so that we may understand a ministry to have been laid upon us. Therefore it is no more said to me than to you. The Pope: Therefore, I will stir up wars. But (on the Expositor's or Bellarmine's reading) it does not mean that the Prophet should wage war. The Pope: Therefore I, reigning on high over kings, etc. Bernard: Rather, the words sound of ministry, not of dominion. The Pope: Therefore, I will take kingdoms from others and confer them on others, as Lord of kings, because I have a figure in the Prophet. Bernard: You are mistaken; this is not an imperial or political figure but a figure of spiritual and, as it were, rustic labour; nor are you more than a Prophet. The Pope: Yet I will do this, therefore, because it is in relation to God and contributes a spiritual good. Bernard: If you are wise, you will be content with your measure, for whatever is more than that is of evil.

units.la: In hac Consideratione Bernardi (nam tantum de Expositione huius scripturae contendimus) quis non Papam obseruet nullum non Tyrannidis praetextum sibi arripere ex illis Prophetae verbis, quae (vt ait Bernardus) nihil fastus sonant? Nec Bernardus solùm, sed & longè antè illum Gregorius Magnus Papa, & Hieronymus, & ex antiquis Patribus, quotquot huius Scripturae mentionem fecerint, Propheticè dictum interpretantur; nimirum, Muneris esse Ministrorum Praedicare, & denunciare iudicia Dei aduersus praefractos & contumaces; non autem debere ipsos ab aliis Poenas temporales exigere: quod & Maldonatus Iesuita nuper agnouit; [vt euellas] &c. Idest (inquit) si non respuerint Iudaei nunciabis fore vt ego (Dominus) eos euellam, destruam, perdam---si autem respuerint, nunciabis fore vt aedificem, plantem, id est, bene eis faciam. Haec ille. Enimuero ex his Prophetae verbis Pontifices, si minus Eradicandi, & Extirpandi Reges impios; annon tamen Excommunicandi potestatem eliciant? nè id quidem; nam quicquid Iurisdictionis in veteri lege obseruare licet, non Prophetis id competebat, sed tantùm penes Sacerdotes fuit: quo quid male-sanos istos Glossatores (nimirùm Pontifices) crassioris caecitatis arguat? Hactenùs de interpretatione huius Scripturae; quae tamen quo animo abs Te, Bellarmine proferatur, tùm facilius intelligemus, si adiunxeris testimonium aliquod clarius.
units.tr: In this Consideration of Bernard (for we are contending only about the interpretation of this passage) who does not observe that the Pope seizes on every pretext of tyranny from those words of the Prophet which, as Bernard says, sound of no pride? Not only Bernard, but also, long before him, Gregory the Great, the Pope, and Jerome, and all the ancient Fathers who have made mention of this Scripture, interpret it prophetically: namely, that it is the duty of ministers to preach and to announce the judgements of God against the stubborn and the obstinate, but that they ought not themselves to exact temporal penalties from others. This the Jesuit Maldonatus also has recently acknowledged: [that you should pluck up] etc. That is (he says): if the Jews do not repent, you will announce that I (the Lord) will pluck them up, destroy them, and ruin them; but if they repent, you will announce that I will build and plant them, that is, do them good. So he. Indeed, from these words of the Prophet, do the Popes not draw out, if not the power to eradicate and extirpate impious kings, at least the power to excommunicate? Not even that; for whatever jurisdiction may be observed in the old law did not belong to the Prophets, but rested only with the priests. What does this prove about those mad glossators (the Popes, that is) except a cruder blindness? So much for the interpretation of this Scripture; yet with what purpose it is put forward by you, Bellarmine, we shall understand more easily if you add some clearer testimony.

units.la: Bellarminus de Offic.
units.tr: Bellarmine, De Offic.

units.la: "Quod item clarius explicat Ezechiel, dicens, [factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens, fili hominis, speculatorem dedi te domui Israël, & audies de ore meo verbum, &."
units.tr: "What Ezekiel also explains more clearly, saying: the word of the Lord came to me, saying, son of man, I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel, and you shall hear the word from my mouth, etc."

units.la: “ enunciabis eis ex me.[?] Si dicente me ad impium morte morieris, non annunciaueris ei, neque loquutus fueris, vt auertatur à via sua mala, & viuat, ipse Impius in iniquitate sua morietur, sanguinem autem eius de manu tua requiram. Si autem annunciaueris Impio, & ille non fuerit conuersus ab impietate sua, ipse quidem in impietate sua morietur, Tu autem animam tuam liberasti. Ezech. 3.] Hæc ipsa, quæ Dominus de Prophetis, qui prædicatores illius temporis erant, dicit, eadem omninò intelligi debent de Episcopis, ad quos præcipuè pertinet officium prædicationis. — pag.32.33.
units.tr: "you shall declare it to them from me. If, when I say to the wicked man, you shall surely die, you do not warn him, nor speak so that he turns from his evil way and lives, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood at your hand. But if you warn the wicked man, and he is not turned from his wickedness, he shall die in his wickedness, but you have delivered your soul. Ezek. 3.] These very things which the Lord says of the Prophets, who were the preachers of that time, must be wholly understood of the bishops, to whom the office of preaching chiefly belongs." — pp. 32, 33.

units.la: L. ANIMADVERSIO.
units.tr: First Animadversion

units.la: Prophetam[?] & Papam, quoad officium speculandi, longe interualle inter se distare.
units.tr: That the Prophet and the Pope, as regards the office of watching, are far apart from one another.

units.la: CLarius repera Propheta loquitur, quàm vt pro Pon-tificis tui Primatu (quod tamen vnum * intendis) vel quicquam faciat; imo verò causam Pontificiam planè iugulat. I. quia in veteri Testamento Propheta nullum verbum populo tradit, nisi prius à Dei ore acceptum; id quod Apostolus exemplo suo docuit in nouo : {q}Quod (inquit) accepi à Domino tradidi vobis. Antecedat, oportet, [illegible, ~2 words], sequatur [illegible, ~1 word]. At ex scrinio pectoris Pontificis, tanquam ex falsorum Commentariorum, & chirographorum officina, Articuli noui, seu noua Testamenta, indices prodeunt. II. Propheta Ezechiel delinquentes, morte dignos, acerrimè est persecutus; sed mortem à Deo definitam, minando tantum, ac denunciando, non autem machinando, vt Papa Hildebrandus; & illius exemplo, Pontifices post Eum alij factitarunt. III. Prophetæ illius temporis (inquis) Prædicatores fuerunt; certè, & prædicandi munus fideliter exquiri sunt: quod tàm sacrum munus * Papa iamdiu negotijs secularibus, ludis, & omne genus voluptatibus posthabuit. Verè Tu admodùm, Bellarmine, Prophetæ sensum explicuisti ; de quo fortè haud magnam apud Romanenses initurus es gratiam.
units.tr: Clearer than the Prophet speaks, it does nothing for the primacy of your Pope (which nonetheless you are aiming at); indeed it utterly cuts the throat of the Papal cause. First, because in the Old Testament the Prophet delivers no word to the people unless he has first received it from the mouth of God; which the Apostle taught by his own example in the New: What I received from the Lord, I delivered to you. [illegible, ~2 words] must go before, [illegible, ~1 word] must follow. But from the strongbox of the Pope's breast, as from a workshop of forged commentaries and handwritings, come forth new articles, or new testaments, as indexes. Second, the Prophet Ezekiel pursued the offenders, those worthy of death, most sharply; but he threatened and announced death as decreed by God, without devising it, as Pope Hildebrand did; and after his example the other Popes who followed have done likewise. Third, you say the Prophets of that time were preachers; certainly, and the duty of preaching is to be faithfully sought; yet the Pope has long set aside this so sacred duty in favour of secular business, play, and every kind of pleasure. Truly, Bellarmine, you have explained the sense of the Prophet very well; though perhaps you will not win much favour among the Romanists by doing so.

units.la: IV. Dic, verò præterea si possis, vbi vel Speculatorem Ecclesiæ Rom. vel Speculantem ipsam Ecclesiam quis reperiet, quando Pontifices, Ecclesiáque illa vniuersa per Annos aliquot tàm grandi lethargo laborabat, vt Baronius ad mentionem eius horreat, & in Temporum illorum [illegible, ~5 letters] & infelicitatem vehementer inuehatur. {f}Que tunc facies sanctæ Rom. Ecclesiæ? (inquit) quam fœdissima, cùm Romæ dominarentur potentissimæ æquè ac sordidissimæ meretrices ; quarum arbitrio intruderentur in sedem Petri earum Amasii pseudo-Pontifices ; --- quandò in eligendo Pontifice Traditiones veteres, & sacra consuetudines prorsus extincta: --- Dormiebat tunc planè alto, vt apparet, Christus in navi, dum ista non videre se dissimulans, sineret sic fieri, dum non exurgeret vindex. Et, quod & deterius videbatur, deerant qui Dominum sic dormientem clamoribus excitarent, discipulis strertentibus[?] omnibus. Qualesnam, reris, delectos ab his monstris Cardinales fuisse? --- imitatos esse ipsos, sectatosq; eorum vestigia quis non facilè credat? & optâsse hos omnes Dominum dormisse semper, & nunquam in iudicium surrecturum? Hæc Ille, de Illis, quos PseudoPontifices vocat; quos tamen eo tempore pro veris & legitimis habitos esse concedit. O egregios Dominici gregis Speculatores scilicet! Quorum tamen authoritatem, præ Episcopis aliis, Tu ex loco nescio quò prærogatiuæ atque eminentiæ gradu amplificare conaris.
units.tr: Fourth, tell me, if you can, where anyone will find a watchman of the Roman Church, or the Church itself watching, at a time when the Popes and that whole Church laboured under so great a lethargy for some years that Baronius shudders at the mention of it, and inveighs vehemently against the wretchedness and unhappiness of those times. What face then had the holy Roman Church? he says, how most foul, when the most powerful and at the same time most filthy harlots ruled at Rome; by whose will their lovers, pseudo-popes, were thrust into the seat of Peter; — when, in electing a Pope, the ancient traditions and sacred customs were utterly extinguished; — Christ, it seems, was then sleeping deeply in the boat, while those who pretended not to see these things allowed them to happen so, and did not rise up as avenger. And, what seemed worse still, there were none who would rouse the sleeping Lord with their cries, all the disciples snoring. What sort of men, do you suppose, were the Cardinals chosen by these monsters? — who would not easily believe that they imitated them and followed in their footsteps? and that all of them wished the Lord would always sleep and never rise to judgement? So he, speaking of those whom he calls pseudo-popes, yet whom he concedes were at that time held to be true and lawful. Oh, excellent watchmen of the Lord's flock, indeed! Yet their authority, above the other bishops, you try to magnify from I know not what rung of precedence and eminence.

units.la: Bellarminus de Offic.
units.tr: Bellarmine, De Officio

units.la: « Episcoporum autem Caput, & Princeps est summus Pontifex. --- Pag. 33.
units.tr: « The head and prince of the bishops, however, is the supreme Pontiff. --- Page 33.

units.la: Explicatio.
units.tr: Explanation.

units.la: Non hæc ad Episcopos tantum castigandos dixti ; nam de ipso fidelium omnium, adeoque Regum Christianorum Capite agitur :. quod Attributum nè quid sinistri[?] portendat ominis nimis vereor. {t}Etiam Petro (inquis) ostensa est visio de electione gentium, vbi (Act. 10.) pulchrè dicitur, [Macta, & manduca:] nam Capitis est manducare, & per manducationem trajicere in stomachum, & sibi incorporare. Itaper Metaphoram Petri erat infideles convertere. Audio, sed ex Titulo, & visione isthac quid tandem colligis? (I) {u}Ex his praerogatiuis demonstratur Primatus Petri. Esto, sed quid hoc ad Pontificem? Ergo (II) {x}Vnio membrorum cum Capite (videlicet, Romano Pontifice) est Nota Ecclesiae. Ergo (III) {y}Papa non adfuit personaliter primis Concilijs generalibus, quia non videbatur convenire, vt caput sequeretur membra. Ergo (IV) {z}Pontifex non potuit submittere se coactiue sententiae Conciliorum vt deponatur. {a}Quia praestat caput aegrum habere, quàm nullum: nec consulunt Medici vt caput, aegrum licet, tollamus, vt ab aegritudine liberemur.
units.tr: I did not say these things only to rebuke bishops; the matter concerns the head of all the faithful, and so of Christian kings as well. I greatly fear that this attribute portends something ominous. Peter too (you say) was shown a vision about the election of the Gentiles, where (Acts 10) it is nicely said, [Kill and eat]: for it belongs to the head to eat, and by eating to pass food into the stomach and make it part of oneself. So by this metaphor it was Peter's task to convert unbelievers. I hear you, but from this title and this vision what do you finally conclude? (I) From these prerogatives the primacy of Peter is demonstrated. Granted, but what does this have to do with the Pontiff? Therefore (II) union of the members with the Head (namely the Roman Pontiff) is a mark of the Church. Therefore (III) the Pope was not personally present at the first general councils, because it did not seem fitting that the head should follow the members. Therefore (IV) the Pontiff could not submit himself to the coercive judgment of the councils so as to be deposed. Because it is better to have a sick head than none; nor do physicians advise removing the head, even a diseased one, so that we may be freed from the sickness.

units.la: I. ANIMADVERSIO.
units.tr: I. Animadversion.

units.la: Papam, quâ (ex interpretatione Pontificiorum) Caput dicitur, reliquis membris heterogeneum; & à corpore Ecclesiae, cùm Ratio tulerit, amputandum esse.
units.tr: The Pope, who (by the Papists' interpretation) is called the Head, is foreign in kind to the other members, and must be cut off from the body of the Church, since reason requires it.

units.la: Primò, Ad Tuum, de Visione Petri, interpretamentum quod spectat; quis Theologus sanae mentis responso Te dignaretur: quia si vox illa [Manduca] probat Pontificem esse Caput, partem nimirùm Corporis nobilissimam; certè vox [Macta] (nam manuum est mactare) deprimit Eum rursus, aliosque Episcopos, velut Ecclesiae humeris substituit.
units.tr: First, as to your interpretation of Peter's vision: what theologian of sound mind would deign to answer you? For if that word [Eat] proves that the Pontiff is the Head, the most noble part of the body, then certainly the word [Kill] (for killing is the work of hands) again lowers him, and the other bishops with him, and sets them, as it were, on the shoulders of the Church.

units.la: II. Vnionem cum Capite, Pontifice, Ecclesiae Notam esse; admittere non audemus, nè Vnionem nostram cum antiquissimis, celeberrimis, Catholicissimisque Ecclesijs Ecclesijs abiuremus, quae Papalem *Excommunicationem flocci fecerunt. Deinde non eò stuporis deuenimus, vt Vnionem cum Rom. Ecclesiae Capite verae & Catholicae Ecclesiae Notam veram & indubitatam esse credamus, cùm praesertim Caput ipsum saepius per se tam penitus ignotum tum fuerit, vt etiam Corpus ipsum (quæ est Rom. Ecclesia) se nonnunquàm [illegible, ~10 letters], aliquandò [illegible, ~8 letters], sæpè [illegible, ~8 letters] esse dolenter deplorauerit. I. quia cùm vt {b}Pontificij bene multi definiunt) Hæreticus fit extra Ecclesiam, ac proinde Ecclesiæ membrum non habetur: Igitur (nempè Papa Hæreticus) dici non potest Ecclesiæ caput, quia membrum non est. II. quia Romana Ecclesia sæpè biceps, interdùm, etiam triceps, à {c}Tribus simul capitibus regebatur. III. quia omninò destituta fuit suo Capite, sede vacante per duos, aut tres Annos; aliquandò verò, {d}Annos septem, atque etiam {e}Octo simul.
units.tr: II. We dare not admit that union with the Head, the Pontiff, is a mark of the Church, lest we renounce our union with the most ancient, most celebrated and most Catholic churches, which made light of the Papal excommunication. Further, we have not come to such stupidity as to believe that union with the head of the Roman Church is a true and indubitable mark of the true and Catholic Church, especially since the Head itself has so often been so thoroughly unknown in itself, and the Body itself (which is the Roman Church) has at times [illegible], at other times [illegible], and often [illegible], and has lamented this with grief. First, because, as many Papists define, a heretic is outside the Church, and so is not counted a member of the Church: therefore (namely a heretical Pope) cannot be called the head of the Church, because he is not a member. Second, because the Roman Church was often two-headed, and sometimes even three-headed, being ruled by three heads at once. Third, because it was wholly deprived of its head, the see being vacant for two or three years; and at times for seven years, and even for eight at once.

units.la: IV. Papam, dixi, non interfuisse Concilijs Generalibus, quia videbatur ipsi Celsitudine suâ indignum; vt Caput sequeretur membra. Deus bone! quam tu Ecclesiæ heterogeneum Caput depingis, veluti quis cerulci humanæ Caput adiungat Equinum? Spectatum admissi [?] Imò non irridendus es, Bellarmine; miserandus magis, quoniam quasi veri membri sensum omnem perdidisses, non sentis quòd {f}Quantumuis (vt rectè vester Ferus) membrum vnum altero nobilius sit, nihilominus tamen hoc esse omnibus commune, quòd sint membra corporis eiusdem, in hoc vnum non præstare aliý, vnum alteri non inuidere, nec inferius contemnere: atque eodem modo in Ecclesia quodlibet membrum suâ operatione aliis inseruire. Exemplum habetis in Petro Act. 8. qui ab Apostolis missus cum Iohanne in Samariam, Eorum mandatis obtemperauit, & Apostolicam legationem gnauiter est executus. Vestrum {g}vero Caput (Rom. Pontifex) existimabat Non sibi conuenire, vt membra sua sequeretur. Serum Seruorum Dei, scilicet.
units.tr: IV. I said the Pope was not present at the General Councils because it seemed beneath his dignity, so that the head should follow the members. Good God! What a foreign head you paint for the Church! As if someone should attach a horse's head to a human body! [Spectatum admissi?] Indeed, Bellarmine, you are not to be mocked but rather pitied, since, as if you had lost all sense of a true member, you do not perceive that however much one member may be nobler than another (as your Ferus rightly says), still this is common to all, that they are members of the same body: that one does not claim superiority over the others in this, does not envy another, nor scorn the lower; and in the same way in the Church each member serves the others by its activity. You have an example in Peter, Acts 8, who, sent with John by the Apostles into Samaria, obeyed their commands and diligently carried out the apostolic mission. But your Head (the Roman Pontiff) thought it did not befit him to follow his own members. Servant of the servants of God, forsooth.

units.la: Postremò argutulum tuum Argumentum, quo probas Papam qualemcunque non posse Deponi coactiuâ vllâ potestate, quia consultis Medicis, Caput, ægrum licet, tolerandum est; iamdudùm exsibilàrunt Concilij Basileensis Theologi, & Capitis vestri Eugenij Medici Ecclesiastici. {h}Quamuis (inquiunt) nunquàm suadeant Medici, vt Caput, quamuis ulcerosum, abscindatur: --- tamen si perinde ut in Corpore mystico, uno capite submoto, possit aliud inueniri, nunquid non sepissime ob vanas aegritudines capita mutarentur? --- imo etiam (nempe in Corpore Ecclesiastico) utile erit interdum & necessarium, --- ut Hieronymus dotet, cum de Praelato fatuo; Sal (inquit) infatuatum nullo usui inseruit, nisi mittatur foras. Haec de Pontifice, quatenus Caput dicitur; ad Speculatorem redeamus.
units.tr: Finally, your clever argument, by which you prove that the Pope, whatever sort he is, cannot be deposed by any coercive power, because when physicians are consulted the head, though sick, must be borne, has long since been hissed at by the theologians of the Council of Basel and by the ecclesiastical physicians of your head, Eugenius. Although (they say) physicians never advise cutting off the head, however ulcerous it may be: yet if, just as in the mystical body, one head being removed another can be found, would not heads very often be changed on account of trivial sicknesses? Indeed even (namely in the ecclesiastical body) it will sometimes be useful and necessary, as Jerome teaches when speaking of a foolish prelate: "Salt that has lost its savour is of no use, unless it is cast out." Thus far concerning the Pontiff, insofar as he is called the Head; let us return to the Speculator.

units.la: Bellarminus de Offic.
units.tr: Bellarmine, De Officiis

units.la: “ Solebant autem Pontifices maximi, & Episcopi reliqui, qua “ mala ex specula cernebant, in Concionibus ad praesentes, “ per literas ad absentes pronunciare. --- Pag.33.
units.tr: “The supreme Pontiffs and the other bishops used, from the watchtower, to announce the evils they saw, to those present in sermons and to those absent by letter.” — p. 33.

units.la: I. ANIMADVERSIO.
units.tr: First Observation.

units.la: Papam etiamsi Speculatorem praeferat, Speculam tamen ipsam iam olim demisisse.
units.tr: Even if the Pope is called the watchman, he has long ago let down the watchtower itself.

units.la: Pontifices autem vestri, ut plerique etiam Episcopi posterioris aetatis, Concionari ad praesentes soliti non sunt: {*}Quotus enim quisque Praelatorum maiorum minorumue populum suum docere videtur? proinde {‡}Authores aliqui Pontificij, nec hos inter Pastores; nec Illos inter istos Maximos Pontifices numerandos esse censuerunt: quomodo enim ex pulpito, veluti ex specula, praesentes cernere Pontifex poterit, qui ipse in hac Specula nunquam cernitur? quique praesentes negligit, quomodo speculationis fidem erga absentes praestabit? Solebant (inquis) Pontifices maximi ad praesentes concionari. Verisimile esse quis autumet, aliquam tibi simulatatem [?] cum posteris Pontificibus intercessisse, quod, ad horum negligentiam damnandam, voce illa tua SOLEBANT Illorum curam fidemque introduxeris? dum Tu Speculator quidem, & velut ex Tarpeio culmine cornix,
units.tr: But your Pontiffs, like most bishops of the later age, were not in the habit of preaching to those present: {*}For how few of the greater or lesser prelates seem to teach their people? Therefore some Papist authors have judged that neither should these be counted among the ministers, nor those among these supreme Pontiffs. For how can a Pontiff see those present from the pulpit, as if from a watchtower, when he himself is never seen in this watchtower? And one who neglects those present, how will he keep the faith of a watchman towards those absent? The supreme Pontiffs, you say, used to preach to those present. Who would think there was some similarity between you and the later Pontiffs, so that by that word of yours, WERE, you introduced their care and faithfulness, in order to condemn their negligence? While you, indeed a Watchman, like a crow from the Tarpeian height,

units.la: SVNT, quia non possis dicere; dicis, ERANT.
units.tr: ARE, because you cannot say so; you say, WERE.

units.la: Haec de Pontificii Specula, quoad Praesentes; sequitur quoad Absentes.
units.tr: This is the Papists' watchtower as regards those present; there follows what it is as regards those absent.

units.la: {*} Espenceus [?] vid. supra cap. 2. §.17.
units.tr: {*} Espenceus [?], see above, chap. 2, §17.

units.la: {‡} Espenceus [?] ibid.
units.tr: {‡} Espenceus [?], ibid.

units.la: Bellarminus de Ossic.
units.tr: Bellarmine, De Officiis.

units.la: “ Hinc S. Ambrosius in Epistola ad Theodosium Imperatorem scribit, se non posse vllo modo tacere, si qua mala facta de ipso audiuerit; & ideo aequo animo ferat reprehensiones suas. --pag. 33.
units.tr: “Hence St Ambrose writes in his Epistle to the Emperor Theodosius that he cannot in any way keep silent if he hears of any evil deeds of his, and therefore he should bear his rebukes with equanimity.” — p. 33.

units.la: I. AINMADVERSIO. Ambrosij diuinissimi viri Exemplum imitationem [?] esse.
units.tr: First Observation. The example of the most divine man Ambrose is to be imitated.

units.la: Ambrosius verus Pastor fuit, vtpote qui in Concionibus habendis versatissimus fuit, & pene dominabatur: vestri autem Pontifices sibi quasi indixerunt, imperarunt-que silentium. Ille vir vndique sanctissimus praeclaram hanc vocem, & viro Apostolico dignam, de se merito pronunciare potuit; Non ita vixi, vt pudeat me diutius viuere, nec metuo mori, quia bonum Dominum habeo [?]: ita vt & clarius aliorum vitia cernere, & liberius corripere potuerit. At Pontifices (quales permultos suisse vos fatemini) omnium vitiorum sordibus contaminatissimi, qui potuerint peccata aliorum reprehendere, nisi in opprobrium sui? Deinde Principes Theodosios debere, imò velle quoque aequo animo ferre se, quoties iusta causa subest, ab Ambrosij suis reprehendi, iuxta tecum sentimus: at, in Principibus reprehendendis, inter Pontificem & Ambrosium quam dispar sit ratio vides. Quorsum vero tandem, quae de Episcoporum officio narras, omnia?
units.tr: Ambrose was a true minister, since he was most practised in preaching and almost held sway over his hearers; but your Pontiffs have, as it were, declared silence on themselves and enjoined it on others. That most holy man could justly pronounce of himself this famous saying, worthy of an apostolic man: I have not lived in such a way as to be ashamed to live longer, nor do I fear to die, because I have a good Lord [?]. So he could both see the vices of others more clearly and rebuke them more freely. But the Pontiffs (such as you admit there were very many of) were most defiled by the filth of every vice: how could they have rebuked the sins of others except to their own shame? Next, you say, and we agree with you, that the Emperor Theodosius ought, indeed ought also to wish to bear with equanimity, whenever a just cause lies behind it, to be rebuked by his Ambrose; but you see how unequal the reckoning is between the Pontiff and Ambrose in rebuking princes. Yet to what end, finally, are all these things you say about the office of bishops?

units.la: Bellarminus de Offic.
units.tr: Bellarmine, De Officiis.

units.la: “ Quae cum ita sint, & Episcopi, & Principis Episcoporum, cuius totius mundi Dioecesis est, debent igitur Principes. &c. — pag. 33.
units.tr: “Since these things are so, both bishops and the Prince of bishops, whose diocese is the whole world, ought therefore to be [princes]. etc.” — p. 33.

units.la: Explicatio.
units.tr: Explanation.

units.la: Quid hoc portenti est? Papa Princeps Episcoporum; Papa etiam Dicecesis totum mundum ambitu suo complectitur? Res haec maioris momenti est, quam vt debeat à Nobis leuiter attingi: video enim Totius mundi Dioecesin à Papa vendicari, non solùm (vt hic) respectu Episcoporum, sed & omnium Principum. De priori respectu hic agitur; de altero forsan alius erit dicendi locus. Age igitur huiusce tàm universalis Dioecefeos rationem aliquam expone. {k} Quis ex nominibus, ex quibus Pontificis primatus colligitur, unum est hoc, universalis Episcopus, quod Pontifici Romano tribui solet. {l} Nam Leo Papa Episcopus Universalis inscribitur in Concilio Chalcedonensi Act. 3.
